title: At the Hotel: Checking In
summary: In this lesson, you will learn how to check into a hotel and ask for help at the front desk. These simple phrases will make your trip easy and comfortable.

sections.p: When you arrive at a hotel, you need to talk to the person at the front desk. You give them your name and your passport. You can use polite phrases like 'I have a reservation' to tell them you booked a room before you came.

ex.en: I have a reservation for two nights.
ex.mean: I booked a room here for two days.
I am here to get my room key.

sections.p: After you check in, you might want to know important details about your stay. You can ask about breakfast time and the Wi-Fi password. Use 'What time' for schedules and 'Is breakfast' to check if food is included.

ex.mean: When can I eat the morning meal?
Do I have to pay extra for food?
How do I connect to the internet?

sections.p: Sometimes you need extra things in your room, like a towel or a quieter space. You can use the polite phrase 'Could I have' to ask the staff for help. Always remember to say 'Thank you'!

ex.en: Could I have an extra towel, please?
ex.mean: Please give me one more towel.
How do I find the elevator?

ex.en: Can you help me with my bags?
ex.mean: Please help me carry my luggage.

tip: Practice saying these phrases out loud before your trip. Imagine you are talking to the hotel worker so you feel ready and relaxed!
